title: MOFA thanks leaders of five allied nations for supporting Taiwan’s participation at COP31
text:
Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung sincerely thanks the leaders of five allied nations who voiced firm support for Taiwan’s participation in global climate governance mechanisms at the leaders’ summit of the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31).

COP31 was held in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20. During the leaders’ summit, which was held on November 11 and 12, Marshall Islands President Hilda C. Heine; Palau President Surangel S. Whipps, Jr.; Eswatini Prime Minister Russell Mmiso Dlamini; Tuvalu Prime Minister Feleti Penitala Teo; and Saint Christopher and Nevis Deputy Prime Minister Geoffrey Hanley spoke up for Taiwan’s inclusion.

President Heine stated that all voices must be heard, including those of Taiwan. She emphasized that as Taiwan was decoupling economic growth from carbon emissions, implementing a just transition, and strengthening climate resilience, it should have been participating in the conference.

President Whipps declared that Palau, as a maritime nation, deeply understood the need for everyone to embrace a spirit of shared destiny and joint efforts. He noted that Taiwan was a strong and important partner and a leader in disaster resilience, energy transition, and food security, adding that the world needed Taiwan’s participation at COP. He also said that countries all shared this planet and that they were strongest when they paddled together.

Prime Minister Dlamini pointed out that Taiwan and Japan offered valuable lessons in resilient infrastructure, early warning systems, and disaster preparedness. He stated that Taiwan’s expertise should be available to the common endeavor to protect lives and livelihoods, that climate change surpassed national boundaries, and that cooperation must rise to the same universal challenge. He reiterated Eswatini’s support for Taiwan’s meaningful participation in relevant international climate change processes.

Prime Minister Teo stated that climate change knew no political boundaries and neither should climate action. He also commended Taiwan’s contributions to global climate efforts and said that no willing partner should be left behind.

Deputy Prime Minister Hanley stressed that acknowledging Taiwan’s practical contributions to such areas as environmental governance, the circular economy, climate resilience, green energy, and capacity building was critical. Moreover, he said that his country continued to benefit from its partnership with Taiwan in these areas.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs sincerely thanks these allied countries for their unwavering support of Taiwan’s participation in global climate governance mechanisms.

Taiwan will continue to strive to fulfill its responsibilities as a member of the international community and work closely with allies and like-minded partners to jointly address climate change. （E）
